label: anther wing
reason: The class and its definition are correct. In Asclepiadoideae (and Secamonoideae) each anther has hard, membranous to cartilaginous side wings, and two neighbouring wings frame the guide rail (the stigmatic slit) that leads the pollinator's leg to the corpusculum. The parent (cardinal organ part, part of anther) fits. The problem is the exact synonym 'guide rail wing': the guide rail is the slit formed by a PAIR of wings from neighbouring anthers, not one wing, and the phrase is not standard glossary usage. Move it to related synonyms or drop it. 'anther flange' can stay as an exact synonym.

label: false vein
reason: This matches fern usage: false veins (false veinlets, spurious veins) are strands of long, often thick-walled cells in the leaf blade that are not connected to the true veins and carry no vascular tissue. They are typical of Hymenophyllaceae (e.g. Didymoglossum, Crepidomanes, often running inside the margin) and some Adiantum (Pteridaceae). The definition follows the genus-differentia form, and the parent and part-of (cardinal organ part of a phyllome lamina; leaf lamina is a kind of phyllome lamina) fit. 'false veinlet' and the French 'fausse nervure' work as exact synonyms, and 'pseudovein' fits as a related one. The phrase 'not connected to the vascular system and without vascular tissue' is slightly repetitive but correct.

label: fruit beak
reason: The definition is botanically correct: the beak (rostrum) is a narrowed, prolonged tip of the fruit. In Brassicaceae it is the seedless top of the silique, in Cyperaceae it comes from the persistent style base, in Lactuceae it is the stalk-like neck of the cypsela, and the stylar beak of Geraniaceae also fits. A cardinal organ part is the right parent, rather than PO 'fruit distal end' (PO_0008001), which is a region and not a projection. The problem is that 'achene beak' is listed as an exact synonym. It names only the beak of an achene or cypsela, so it is narrower than 'fruit beak' (silique beaks are not achene beaks) and should be a narrow synonym. 'beak', 'rostrum' and 'bec' are rightly related synonyms, since they also apply to perigynium, keel and operculum beaks.
